title: Overview
objective: Establish the scope, goals, and reference baseline for the full engine replacement project on VIN WBAFF01070L319611.
warnings: This manual is a personal project workspace, not an official BMW repair manual. Always cross-reference safety-critical values against BMW TIS/ISTA before acting on them.

steps.text: Record full vehicle identification: 2009 BMW X5 E70 xDrive35d, engine M57TU2D30 (306D5), VIN WBAFF01070L319611.
Document the failure: engine failure with crankshaft and connecting rod bearing damage confirmed. Photograph any evidence (metal in oil, oil pan debris, etc.).
Decide on replacement strategy: complete used engine swap vs. short block rebuild. This manual assumes a replacement engine swap.
Set up this app as the single source of truth: enter parts, tools, budget, and timeline before starting teardown.
Walk the vehicle and take baseline photos of exterior, interior, engine bay, and undercarriage for a before/after record.

title: Safety
objective: Set up a safe working environment before any wrenching begins.
warnings: Never work under a vehicle supported only by a jack — always use rated jack stands.
Diesel fuel system operates at very high pressure — relieve pressure per procedure before opening any line.
Disconnect the battery before working on wiring, fuel injection, or airbag-adjacent components.
Diesel exhaust and running engines in an enclosed garage can cause carbon monoxide buildup — ensure ventilation.

steps.text: Clear a dedicated workspace with good lighting and ventilation.
Stage fire extinguisher and first aid kit within reach.
Confirm engine hoist and jack stand ratings exceed the loads you'll apply.
Establish a fluid disposal plan (used oil, coolant, fuel) compliant with local regulations.
Set a rule: disconnect battery before any electrical or fuel system work, no exceptions.
Keep a phone charged and reachable at all times when working alone.

checklist: Jack stands rated and positioned correctly
Battery disconnect is standard procedure before wiring/fuel work

title: Tools
objective: Inventory and acquire the tools required for the full project, tracked in the Tools Database.
warnings: Do not substitute torque wrenches with impact guns on safety-critical fasteners (suspension, brakes, engine internals).

steps.text: Review the Tools Database page and mark which tools you already own.
Prioritize required tools over optional tools for the current project phase.
Budget tool purchases into the Budget Tracker under the Tools category.
Verify torque wrenches are calibrated/within their accuracy window before use on safety-critical fasteners.

checklist: Required tools acquired or on order

title: Parts
objective: Establish the parts sourcing and ordering workflow using the Parts Database.
warnings: Always confirm OEM part numbers against the VIN before ordering — E70 diesel variants had running production changes.

steps.text: Review the Parts Database and confirm priority (critical/high/medium/low) for each item.
Cross-reference OEM part numbers using VIN WBAFF01070L319611 via a parts catalog before ordering.
Update part status to 'ordered' when placed, then 'installed' once fitted, to keep dashboard progress accurate.
Log actual prices in the Budget Tracker as parts are purchased.

title: Engine Removal
objective: Safely remove the failed M57TU2D30 engine from the vehicle.
warnings: Engine weight is substantial — never work under a suspended engine.
Relieve fuel system pressure before disconnecting any fuel line.
Label every connector with the Wire Labeling System before disconnecting — this is the single biggest time-saver on reassembly.

steps.text: Follow the Pre-Removal Checklist in full before starting.
Disconnect battery, drain fluids into labeled containers.
Remove front bumper/clip for full engine bay access (see Garage Viewer front-bumper zone).
Remove radiator pack and set aside safely.
Work through the Engine Bay clickable sections systematically, labeling and disconnecting each wiring harness connector.
Disconnect fuel lines (capped immediately) and turbo oil/coolant lines.
Disconnect exhaust downpipe from turbo outlet.
Support transmission independently, then separate bellhousing per torque spec reference TQ-009/TQ-010.
Attach hoist and leveler, remove engine mount bolts (TQ-007/TQ-008), and lift engine clear slowly, watching for snagged lines.
Place engine on stand, photograph thoroughly, and begin the Engine Bay Cleaning chapter.

checklist: Old engine documented with photos for records

title: Engine Bay Cleaning
objective: Deep clean and inspect the empty engine bay before installing the replacement engine.
warnings: Protect remaining electrical connectors and open harness ends from water intrusion during pressure washing.

steps.text: Cover/bag any remaining electrical connectors and open lines.
Apply degreaser, agitate with a brush, and pressure wash the bay.
Inspect subframe, shock towers, and firewall for rust, cracks, or accident damage.
Clean all grounding points to bare, shiny metal.
Inspect the wiring harness for chafing, melted insulation near the turbo, or brittle sections — repair as needed.
Apply touch-up paint or rust treatment to any bare metal spots found.
Dry fully and photograph the clean bay before install.

checklist: Ground points cleaned to bare metal
Harness inspected and repaired if needed

title: Replacement Engine Inspection
objective: Verify the replacement M57TU2D30 engine is sound before it goes into the car.
parts: Main bearing set (if inspecting bottom end)
Rod bearing set (if inspecting bottom end)
warnings: Do not trust seller mileage claims alone — this vehicle's failure started as an unnoticed bearing wear issue. Physically inspect the bottom end regardless of stated condition.

steps.text: Confirm engine code and casting numbers match required application for xDrive35d.
Mount engine on stand and rotate crank by hand — should be smooth with no binding or grinding.
Perform compression or leak-down test on all 6 cylinders.
Drop the oil pan and visually inspect main and rod bearings for scoring, discoloration, or wear.
Inspect timing chain, guides, and tensioner for stretch/wear.
Bench test turbochargers for shaft play and smooth actuator movement.
Test all sensors and glow plugs with a multimeter where possible.
Clean and repaint the exterior of the engine if desired before install.

checklist: Compression/leak-down test passed on all cylinders
Bottom end visually inspected regardless of stated mileage

title: Engine Installation
objective: Install the inspected replacement engine and reconnect all systems.
parts: New fasteners per TIS single-use call-outs
warnings: Never let the transmission hang unsupported on the input shaft during bellhousing mating.
Confirm torque converter is fully seated (measure the gap) before bolting to the flexplate.
Follow the multi-stage torque-to-yield sequence exactly for head bolts and main/rod bearing caps if the bottom end was serviced.

steps.text: Lower engine into the bay slowly with hoist and leveler, aligning to transmission dowels.
Bolt bellhousing per TQ-009 and torque converter per TQ-010.
Install and torque engine mounts per TQ-007/TQ-008 once engine is supported by mounts, not the hoist.
Reconnect every wiring harness connector, matching each to its labeled ID from the Wire Labeling System.
Reconnect all grounding straps per TQ-026 to clean, bare-metal points.
Reinstall fuel system with new seals per the Fuel System chapter.
Reinstall turbo oil/coolant lines and vacuum lines, matching labeled routing.
Reinstall radiator pack and reconnect coolant hoses.
Reinstall front bumper/clip.
Fill all fluids (oil, coolant, transmission) to spec.
Do a final visual sweep of the bay for tools or rags left behind before moving to First Start.

checklist: Engine mounted and torqued per spec
Every wire connector matched to its label and marked reinstalled

title: First Start
objective: Safely bring the replacement engine to life for the first time and verify baseline health.
warnings: Be prepared to shut down immediately at any abnormal noise, warning light, or leak.
Do not rev the engine on first start — idle only, monitoring oil pressure and temperature.
Ensure adequate ventilation for diesel exhaust.

steps.text: Reconnect battery (negative last) and register it via the coding tool.
Turn ignition to position 2 (no crank) and check for expected warning lights and DDE wake-up.
Run a full diagnostic scan and clear any stored faults that are expected from the disconnect (note any that persist).
If possible, crank with fuel/injection disabled briefly to pre-lubricate before a full start (per accepted diesel rebuild practice).
Start the engine and let it idle only — do not rev.
Watch oil pressure and coolant temperature gauges continuously for the first several minutes.
Inspect the entire bay for oil, coolant, fuel, or boost leaks while idling.
Confirm injector correction codes and glow plug cycling via the diagnostic tool.
Shut down, recheck fluid levels, and top up as needed.

checklist: Pre-start diagnostic scan clean or explained
First idle completed with no abnormal noise/leak
Injector codes and glow plug cycle confirmed

title: Cooling System
objective: Service, inspect, and properly bleed the cooling system.
warnings: Never open a hot cooling system — allow full cool-down before removing the expansion tank cap.
Diesel cooling systems on this platform are prone to air pockets — follow the bleed procedure carefully.

steps.text: Drain coolant fully into a clean, labeled container.
Inspect radiator, hoses, thermostat, and water pump per the Engine Bay clickable sections.
Replace any hoses showing softness, swelling, or hardening.
Reassemble with new clamps where reused clamps show fatigue.
Refill with BMW-spec coolant mixed to the correct ratio.
Open the system bleed screw(s) and run the engine at idle/fast idle until air is purged.
Pressure test the system for leaks once bled and topped up.

checklist: All hoses and components inspected/replaced as needed
System refilled with correct coolant spec
Bleed procedure completed with no trapped air
Pressure test passed with no leaks

title: Fuel System
objective: Safely service the high-pressure common-rail diesel fuel system.
warnings: This is a high-pressure diesel common-rail system — extreme cleanliness is required. Any contamination can destroy injectors or the pump.
Relieve system pressure before disconnecting any line.
Cap every open fitting immediately to prevent debris ingress.

steps.text: Relieve fuel system pressure per the procedure noted in the Injectors and Fuel Rail engine bay sections.
Clean the area around all fittings before disconnecting anything.
Disconnect and cap high pressure lines at pump, rail, and injectors.
Remove injectors with a proper puller — never pry.
Record each injector's correction code before it leaves the vehicle.
Install new injector seal washers on every injector, every time.
Torque injector clamp bolts per TQ-016 with angle stage.
Torque fuel rail bolts per TQ-015.
Replace fuel filter.
Prime the system and check for leaks before a full start.
Enter injector correction codes into the ECU via the diagnostic tool.

checklist: System pressure relieved before disconnecting lines
Injector correction codes recorded and re-entered
New seal washers used on every injector
Fittings torqued per spec and leak-checked

title: Turbo System
objective: Inspect, service, and correctly reinstall the sequential twin-turbo system.
warnings: Always prime the oil feed line before first start after turbo work — dry startup rapidly wears bearings.
Do not mix up small (high pressure) and large (low pressure) turbo oil/vacuum line routing.

steps.text: Disconnect and cap oil feed/return lines, label vacuum actuator lines.
Remove exhaust manifold nuts (TQ-011) and separate turbo from manifold.
Inspect for shaft play, oil residue in compressor housing, and smooth actuator movement.
Inspect intercooler core for oil contamination and fin damage.
Reinstall with new gaskets, torque manifold nuts per TQ-011.
Reconnect oil feed line, torque banjo bolt per TQ-012 with new sealing washers.
Reconnect and re-verify vacuum line routing against labels.
Perform a boost/vacuum leak test before first drive.

checklist: Shaft play and actuator movement inspected
New gaskets and sealing washers used
Oil line primed before first start

title: Transmission
objective: Service the ZF 6-speed automatic transmission during the engine-out window.
warnings: Confirm transmission type (automatic vs. manual, if converted) before ordering fluid or parts — this manual assumes the common ZF 6HP26 automatic.

steps.text: With engine out, support transmission independently and confirm it is stable.
Drain transmission fluid into a labeled container.
Replace filter and refill with ZF Lifeguard 6 spec fluid, even though BMW labels it a 'lifetime' fill.
Inspect torque converter seal and pilot bearing area.
Inspect flexplate for cracks before reconnecting bellhousing.
Reconnect per Engine Installation chapter, verifying converter is fully seated before bolt-up.

title: Transfer Case
objective: Inspect and service the xDrive transfer case.
warnings: Check output flange alignment before final torque on transfer case bolts (TQ referenced in Torque Spec Database).

steps.text: Drain and inspect transfer case fluid condition.
Inspect front and rear output flange seals for leaks.
Check transfer case mounting bushings for wear.
Refill with correct spec fluid.
Reconnect to transmission per TQ-023 reference and verify alignment before final torque.

title: Differentials
objective: Inspect and service front and rear differentials.
warnings: Confirm correct limited-slip / open differential fluid spec if applicable before refilling.

steps.text: Drain and inspect fluid from front and rear differentials for metal contamination.
Inspect differential mounts and driveshaft flanges for wear or leaks.
Refill with correct spec fluid to the fill plug level.
Torque driveshaft flange bolts per TQ-024.

checklist: Fluid drained and inspected for metal
Driveshaft flange bolts torqued per TQ-024

title: Suspension
objective: Refresh front and rear suspension components while subframe access is already open.
parts: Front suspension refresh kit (control arms, bushings, ball joints)
warnings: If self-leveling / adaptive suspension is fitted, confirm correct strut/shock variant for this VIN before ordering.
Subframe bolts may be torque-to-yield, single-use — verify in TIS before reusing.

steps.text: Support vehicle securely on rated stands, wheels off.
Inspect control arms, bushings, and ball joints for wear/play.
Replace worn components with the refresh kit.
Torque strut top mount nuts per TQ-017.
Torque ball joint pinch bolts per TQ-018.
Torque subframe bolts per TQ-019 including angle stage if specified.
Perform a post-work alignment check/adjustment.

checklist: All fasteners torqued per spec including angle stages

title: Brakes
objective: Inspect and service the braking system for safe operation.
parts: Brake pad + rotor set (front and rear)
warnings: Brake caliper carrier bolts are safety-critical — always use a torque wrench, never an impact gun.

steps.text: Inspect pads, rotors, and calipers front and rear.
Replace pads/rotors per Parts Database recommendation.
Torque front caliper carrier bolts per TQ-020.
Torque rear caliper carrier bolts per TQ-021.
Bleed brake system and replace fluid.
Test pedal feel and confirm no leaks before road test.

checklist: Pads/rotors inspected and replaced as needed
Caliper bolts torqued with a torque wrench
Pedal feel confirmed firm before driving

title: Steering
objective: Inspect steering components disturbed by engine bay and suspension work.
warnings: Steering column universal joint pinch bolt is safety-critical — torque per TQ-027 and never reuse a damaged bolt.

steps.text: Inspect steering rack boots, tie rod ends, and column universal joint.
Torque steering column pinch bolt per TQ-027 if disturbed.
Check power steering fluid level/condition.
Verify steering wheel centered and no unusual play after reassembly.

checklist: Column pinch bolt torqued per TQ-027 if disturbed
No abnormal play at steering wheel

title: Electrical
objective: Maintain wiring integrity and grounding across the whole project using the Wire Labeling System.
warnings: A single missed ground strap is the most common cause of hard-to-diagnose intermittent faults after an engine R&R.

steps.text: Use the Wire Labeling System to log every connector before disconnecting it anywhere on the car.
Test continuity on all grounding straps after reassembly.
Inspect and test glow plugs individually with a multimeter.
Confirm battery registration after any battery replacement.
Run a full fault code scan after any electrical work as a final check.

checklist: All disturbed connectors logged in Wire Labeling System

title: Coding & Diagnostics
objective: Set up and use BMW diagnostic/coding tools for fault reading, injector coding, and module registration.
tools: OBD / BMW diagnostic interface (ENET or K+DCAN)
Laptop with ISTA-D / ISTA-P or E-Sys
warnings: Coding/flashing operations carry a small risk of module bricking if interrupted — always ensure stable power (battery charger/maintainer connected) during any coding session.

steps.text: Set up ENET or K+DCAN interface with ISTA-D (diagnostics) and/or E-Sys (coding) on a dedicated laptop.
Connect a battery charger/maintainer before any coding session.
Read and log all fault codes before starting any repair for a baseline.
After injector replacement, enter injector correction codes via ISTA/dedicated tool.
After battery replacement, perform battery registration.
After ECU/module work, verify VIN and ISN (immobilizer) data matches the vehicle.
Log all coding actions and results in this chapter's Notes area for future reference.

checklist: Diagnostic interface and software set up
Injector codes entered after injector work

title: Sound System
objective: Plan and execute an audio system upgrade using the Sound System Planner.
warnings: Identify whether a factory amplifier is present before wiring in aftermarket components — bypassing it incorrectly can cause distortion or damage.

steps.text: Document the current/factory system in the Sound System Planner.
Choose an upgrade tier (Factory Baseline / Entry / Mid / Reference).
Plan wiring routes for power, ground, remote turn-on, and signal cabling.
Install amplifier, speakers, and subwoofer per chosen tier.
Label all new wiring using the Wire Labeling System for future serviceability.
Test and tune the system, checking for rattles/panel resonance.

title: Interior Restoration
objective: Refresh interior trim, upholstery, and electronics.
parts: Interior trim refresh kit (leather care + trim clips)
warnings: Disconnect battery before removing any trim panel containing airbag wiring (side curtain, seat-mounted airbags).

steps.text: Deep clean seats, carpets, and headliner.
Inspect leather/upholstery condition and apply conditioner or repair kits as needed.
Replace broken interior trim clips and worn switchgear.
Test all electronics (windows, seats, climate control, infotainment) and log faults for the Coding & Diagnostics chapter.
Document before/after condition with photos.

title: Exterior Restoration
objective: Address exterior bodywork, trim, and panel condition.
warnings: Inspect for prior accident repair or rust before investing in cosmetic work.

steps.text: Inspect all panel gaps and paint condition for signs of prior accident repair.
Check for rust at common E70 trouble spots (rear wheel arches, tailgate, sunroof drains).
Replace damaged or missing exterior trim/clips.
Plan and log required bodywork ahead of Paint Correction chapter.

checklist: Panel gaps and paint condition inspected
Rust checked at common trouble spots

title: Paint Correction
objective: Restore paint clarity and gloss via correction and protection.
parts: Paint correction / detailing consumables (compounds, pads, sealant/ceramic coating)
warnings: Always measure paint thickness before aggressive compounding to avoid burning through clear coat.

steps.text: Wash and clay bar the full exterior.
Measure paint thickness across panels and note any prior repaint areas.
Perform test spot polish to determine correction level needed.
Compound and polish panel by panel.
Apply sealant or ceramic coating for protection.
Photograph final results for the project record.

title: M Sport Conversion
objective: Plan and optionally execute an M Sport aesthetic/handling package conversion.
parts: M Sport bumpers, side skirts, spoiler (sourced separately)
warnings: Confirm parts compatibility with this exact chassis and options (sensors, park distance control cutouts, etc.) before purchase.

steps.text: Define scope: cosmetic-only (bumpers/skirts/wheels) vs. full M Sport suspension conversion.
Source parts matching sensor cutouts (PDC, washer jets) already fitted to this VIN.
Fit exterior components, transferring sensors/hardware from stock parts.
If converting suspension, install M Sport-spec springs/dampers and realign.
Code any relevant options via the diagnostic tool if electronic feature activation is desired.

checklist: Parts confirmed compatible with sensor cutouts

title: Maintenance Schedule
objective: Track ongoing maintenance intervals after the engine replacement is complete.
warnings: Re-torque wheel bolts after the first 50km following any wheel-off work.

steps.text: Log the first-start date and mileage in the Dashboard maintenance log.
Schedule an oil and filter check at ~1,000km after the new engine's first start.
Re-torque wheel bolts at ~50km.
Re-check coolant level and bleed for trapped air after the first few heat cycles.
Set recurring reminders for standard BMW diesel service intervals (oil, fuel filter, air filter) going forward.

title: Fault Code Library
objective: Reference common fault codes relevant to this platform via the Fault Code Library / Torque & Search tools.
warnings: Fault code descriptions in this app are general references — always confirm exact meaning and repair guidance in ISTA for this specific vehicle.

steps.text: Use the Fault Code Library page to search codes as they appear during diagnostics.
Cross-reference common causes listed against your actual symptoms before ordering parts.
Log resolved codes and fixes in the Maintenance Log for future reference.

checklist: Fault Code Library reviewed for any active codes
Root cause confirmed before parts ordered

title: Resources
objective: Central list of reference resources to consult alongside this workshop OS.

steps.text: BMW TIS (Technical Information System) — authoritative source for all torque specs, procedures, and wiring diagrams. VERIFY all safety-critical values here.
ISTA-D / ISTA-P — official BMW diagnostic and programming software.
E-Sys — coding tool for feature activation and module coding.
BMW E70 owner/enthusiast forums and M57TU technical communities — useful for real-world experience, cross-check against TIS before acting.
Local BMW specialist / independent diesel shop — for any step you are not confident performing yourself, especially safety-critical torque-to-yield fasteners.

checklist: Local specialist contact identified for fallback support
